Issue: Exam paper and details readable before the exam window
Risk (in simple words): A candidate can see all questions days early and share them
Suggested Fix: Check publish state and time window in assertAssigned

Issue: Shared default admin password for all new companies and centre users
Risk (in simple words): Anyone who knows one default password can enter every new workspace
Suggested Fix: Invite link + forced password set; remove DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD

Issue: Super admin can delete/deactivate itself (platform lock-out)
Risk (in simple words): One wrong click removes all platform administration
Suggested Fix: Protect super admin rows

Issue: Sessions survive password reset and are stored per user (one refresh token)
Risk (in simple words): A stolen token keeps working after the victim's password is reset
Suggested Fix: Increment tokenVersion and clear refresh hash on password change

Issue: Account lockout can be abused to lock out any user; key not tenant-scoped
Risk (in simple words): Attackers can stop admins and candidates from logging in on exam day
Suggested Fix: Lock by account+IP, add CAPTCHA, include companyId

Issue: Login throttle uses socket IP (proxy) and refresh endpoints are not throttled
How It Was Found/Tested: API tests throttle.proxy, throttle.refresh (second server, limit 10/min) [BE-TC-1283]
Risk (in simple words): Behind a load balancer one attacker blocks everyone; refresh can be brute-forced at full speed
Suggested Fix: trust proxy + req.ip; throttle refresh

Issue: No password strength rule on the API
Risk (in simple words): Easy-to-guess passwords for admins and candidates
Suggested Fix: Shared strength validator

Issue: Inactive account message reveals that the password was correct
Risk (in simple words): Attackers learn valid passwords of disabled accounts
Suggested Fix: Generic error

Issue: JWT secrets are separate per token type and verified with HS256; alg=none and forged tokens rejected
Risk (in simple words): No issue found (positive check)
Suggested Fix: Keep; rotate secrets, use 32+ byte random values

Issue: Tenant isolation holds: every id-based endpoint returns 404 for another company's ids
Risk (in simple words): No issue found (positive check)
Suggested Fix: Keep company scoping in every query; add an automated IDOR test to CI

Issue: Body booleans/numbers converted implicitly ('false' -> true)
Risk (in simple words): Clients can flip flags by sending text; data saved differs from intent
Suggested Fix: Disable implicit conversion for bodies

Issue: Rich text (instructions, questions, messages) is stored without sanitising
Risk (in simple words): Script runs in any app that renders this HTML without escaping (candidate exam app, CKEditor preview)
Suggested Fix: Sanitise HTML on save with an allow-list

Issue: URLs (document fileUrl, company logo/favicon, workspaceUrl) accept javascript: and free text
Risk (in simple words): Links built from these values can run script or point to phishing sites
Suggested Fix: Allow only https URLs or storage keys

Issue: File type check trusts the client MIME type and extension
Risk (in simple words): Malware renamed to .jpg can be stored and shared through presigned links
Suggested Fix: Magic-byte check, size > 0, virus scan

Issue: Uploads are buffered in memory up to 50 MB per request
Risk (in simple words): A few parallel uploads can exhaust server memory
Suggested Fix: Stream to S3 or use presigned uploads only; lower limit

Issue: Uploaded objects are written with Cache-Control public, immutable and a public URL is returned
Risk (in simple words): Candidate documents (ID proof) may be cached publicly if the bucket/CDN is public
Suggested Fix: Private ACL, short presigned GET links, no immutable cache for replaceable keys

Issue: Swagger docs public; health shows DB/Redis
Risk (in simple words): Attackers get a full map of the API
Suggested Fix: Hide docs in production

Issue: CORS allowedHeaders do not include headers the UI sends
Risk (in simple words): Cross-origin deployments break; teams may then 'fix' it with origin '*'
Suggested Fix: Allow the headers or stop sending them

Issue: Helmet headers present: CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, no X-Powered-By
Risk (in simple words): No issue found (positive check)
Suggested Fix: Keep; remove 'unsafe-inline' from script-src when Swagger is off

Issue: Search and filters use parameters; LIKE wildcards escaped
Risk (in simple words): No issue found (positive check)
Suggested Fix: Keep using query builder parameters

Issue: TLS to RDS uses rejectUnauthorized: false
Risk (in simple words): Database traffic can be intercepted by a man-in-the-middle
Suggested Fix: Use the RDS CA bundle and rejectUnauthorized: true

Issue: Secrets have no validation at startup (missing JWT secrets only fail on first use)
Risk (in simple words): App starts with undefined secrets and fails during login, or uses weak secrets
Suggested Fix: Validate env with Joi/zod in ConfigModule.forRoot

Issue: No audit log for logins, deletes, permission and password changes
Risk (in simple words): Incidents cannot be investigated; no trace of who deleted a company
Suggested Fix: Write an audit log table/stream for security events

Issue: 2 critical, 5 high npm advisories (handlebars, proxy-addr, multer, fast-uri, js-yaml)
Risk (in simple words): Known exploitable packages in the server
Suggested Fix: Upgrade NestJS 11.2.7+, npm audit fix
